sentence: This project tests a gene replacement therapy that uses a virus to treat Duchenne muscular dystrophy, a muscle-wasting disease, in canine models.
This project develops methods that detect and measure small molecules and metals in environmental and biological samples.
This project develops treatment strategies for synovial sarcoma, including drugs, an engineered T cell therapy and an mRNA vaccine.
This project studies how proteins help cytotoxic t-cells release the contents of their granules, using human mutations linked to immunodeficiency.
This project studies how young stem cells support neuromuscular health in older adults and which factors they secrete.
This project uses genetic engineering to modify pigs so that their organs might survive transplant into primates.
This project studies how computer-aided diagnosis tools change the viewing behaviors and accuracy of pathologists.
This project studies whether playing a mock musical instrument can correct white matter problems in schizophrenia.
This project builds predictive medicine technology that combines many kinds of data to identify disease causes.
This project studies how non-coding variants change transcriptional regulation and whether they can predict the risk of steatotic liver disease.
This project uses virtual reality experiments to study the neural correlates of fear and tests whether stimulating fear circuitry reduces anxiety-related behaviors.
This project studies whether inhaled exosomes from lung stem cells are safe and effective for treating ischemic heart diseases in animal models.
This project studies how a group of neurons in the hypothalamus senses a fall in glucose and prevents severe hypoglycemia.
This project builds deep learning models that use whole-body MRI to assess tumor burden and forecast disease progression in multiple myeloma.
This project uses molecular simulations to study how an HIV protein changes and helps the virus enter cells.
This project builds machine learning models that sort early atrial fibrillation into types using electronic health records.
This project studies why hematopoietic stem cells with trisomy 21 are more likely to start preleukemia in children with Down syndrome.
This project builds computational tools that use routine CT scans to predict who benefits from immunotherapy for non-small cell lung cancer.
This project runs genetic screens in cultured cells and engineers cell lines to help find cancer targets.
This project studies how the main oncoprotein of Ewing sarcoma and its chromatin surroundings influence each other.
